correctness.rationale: A full analytic proof enumerates all connected star partitions, derives the only potentially binding EF1_outer comparison, optimizes it via the r+1st order statistic, and treats r=0,1 endpoints. The recurrence generates every strict threshold sign while maintaining distinct positive values, giving robust all-pattern realization and the minimum-six-vertex noninterval witness. A standalone direct-definition program passed 49,055 exact comparisons, 1,022 constructed-pattern tests and the explicit witness; experiments are not used as the universal proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The known upper/lower universal guarantee theorems have broader graph classes, but weaker and differently quantified conclusions: they do not classify which agent counts work for a given positive weighted star. A graph-level yes at an agent count implies all single-instance yes there, but star middle counts are graph-level no and consequently impose no restriction on the yes/no pattern of any fixed instance.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new claim neither contradicts nor follows as a corollary of the connected-graph universal spectrum conjecture. The universal star spectrum has a contiguous no block because different witnesses may be used for different counts. The present single witness can have alternating non-guarantee and guarantee instances across agent counts. Neither general bound entails the sorted order-statistic criterion or arbitrary simultaneous strict margins.

value.rationale: The pattern of fairness feasibility as the number of agents varies is a concrete question motivated by graph spectrum research. This exact natural class exhibits every Boolean pattern robustly, even for a simple graph and identical strictly positive valuations. It sharply separates fixed-instance variability from graph-wide guarantee monotonicity, supplies an exact decision criterion, and pins down the smallest possible noncontiguous failure example without relying on arbitrary numerical slices.
